originality.rationale: Motivating article supplies the reset renewal dynamics, but its full main/supplementary analysis gives numerical nondivisibility witnesses and one CP-divisible periodic case, not the all-dimensional operator-order characterization, monotone age-hazard theorem, and explicit decreasing-hazard nonpositive intertwiner. Related papers characterize semi-Markov kernels, trace-distance memory and picture inequivalence without implying this all-unitary noncommuting-reset theorem in their inspected statements. The proof is a new structural specialization based on the last-reset unnormalized operator; database searches did not identify a dominating theorem. Residual possibility of a broader unlocated affine channel theorem remains.
residual_risks: An earlier general theorem for affine unitary-plus-replacement channels might imply the operator-order condition without using resetting language.

value.rationale: Motivated by the exact question posed but not solved analytically in Carollo–Wald: when classical time-dependent renewal resets produce positive/CP-divisible Schrödinger maps. The result gives all-dimensional necessary-and-sufficient operator tests, a checkable universal design guarantee for increasing hazards, a sharp early-time obstruction, and a direct classification of the paper’s rising-ramp protocol. It distinguishes genuine channel positive-indivisibility from universally monotone trace-distance signals; it is not a routine numerical example or parameter-only increment.
